What are the most effective techniques for lateral movement in cloud environments?

Cloud lateral movement differs from traditional AD — identity is the new perimeter. AWS: 1) Stolen IAM credentials → enumerate permissions: aws iam get-account-authorization-details, enumerate via Pacu (cloud exploitation framework). 2) EC2 instance profile role abuse: if you compromise an EC2 instance, curl http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ for instance role credentials. 3) Assuming roles: if role has sts:AssumeRole permissions on other accounts → cross-account lateral movement. 4) Lambda function exploitation: read Lambda env variables for hardcoded credentials. 5) SecretsManager: secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on all secrets dumps all stored credentials. Azure: 1) Managed Identity tokens — similar to AWS instance profiles. 2) Azure CLI tokens stored in ~/.azure/accessTokens.json — steal for lateral movement. 3) Azure VM Run Command — if you have VM Contributor role, execute commands on other VMs. 4) Service Principal credentials in pipelines/repos. GCP: 1) Default service account on GCE has broad permissions — same metadata endpoint. 2) Google access token: gcloud auth print-access-token. 3) Workload Identity allows cross-project access. Tools: Pacu (AWS), AADInternals (Azure AD), ScoutSuite (multi-cloud enumeration), CloudFox (AWS attack path finder).
